def: A template declaration in which the template name is not followed by a template argument list; its template argument list is that of its own template-head. Partial specializations are always relative to the primary template.

The default arguments, noexcept-specifiers, and function contract specifiers of a templated function. For purposes of name lookup and instantiation, they (as well as type-constraints and requires-clauses) are each separate definitions, instantiated on demand.
A template that specifies the layout and operations of an unbounded set of related types; each specialization is a distinct class type.

A declaration of the form `template-name(parameters) -> simple-template-id;` that maps constructor arguments to a class template specialization during class template argument deduction; it is not found by name lookup — all reachable guides are considered.
A template declared within a class or class template (member function templates, member class templates, etc.). A member function template cannot be virtual, and a destructor cannot be a template.
A template parameter that accepts zero or more template arguments, such as `class... Ts`.
A function parameter that accepts zero or more function arguments, such as `Ts... ts`; its declaration is itself a pack expansion.
A lambda capture of the form `...xs = expr`, introducing one init-capture for each element of the pack expansion in the initializer (C++20).
Collective name for template parameter packs, function parameter packs, init-capture packs, and structured binding packs; a pack name may appear only within a pack expansion.

A construct consisting of a pattern and an ellipsis; when instantiated, the pattern is instantiated once for each element of the pack, producing a (possibly empty) list; it may appear only in the contexts enumerated by the standard.

A pack in the pattern of a pack expansion that is not expanded by any nested pack expansion; all unexpanded packs in the same pack expansion must have the same number of elements and are expanded in lockstep.

A class template or variable template declaration in which the template name is followed by an argument list containing template parameters; it provides an alternative definition when the arguments of a specialization match it. Each partial specialization is a distinct template.
A constant template argument in the argument list of a partial specialization that is exactly the name of a constant template parameter; all other constant template arguments are specialized.
Template F is more specialized than G if F is at least as specialized as G and G is not at least as specialized as F; partial specializations are compared by rewriting them as function templates.

Two expressions involving template parameters are equivalent if function definitions containing them would satisfy the ODR (with template parameters renamed by position); compared by token structure, dependent names compare only by name, and lambdas are never equivalent.

Two non-equivalent expressions involving template parameters that yield the same result for any template arguments (or, for unevaluated operands, perform the same operations); template-heads that accept the same set of arguments. Being functionally equivalent but not equivalent results in IFNDR.

When several function templates can all generate viable specializations, the process of determining which is more specialized by transforming the templates with synthesized unique types and deducing in both directions; if deduction succeeds in both directions, constraints decide.
The name of a family of types declared by `template<...> using N = type;`; its specializations are equivalent to the substituted types, it cannot be specialized, and it cannot be deduced from a type.
